FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by 
the Organic Chemicals, Alcohols and Allied Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the Petroleum, 
Coal and Related Products Division Council. 


Terephthalic acid (CsH604) is derived by oxidation of p-xylene using soluble bromide, metal acetates and acetic 
acid solvent. It is also commercially known as p-phthalic acid; benzene-p-dicarboxylic acid or 1,4- 
benzenedicarboxylic acid. It is represented by the following structural and molecule formulae: 


COOH 


COOH 


Molecular weight : 166 
[Molecular formula : CH4 (COOH) 2] 


It is used in the production of synthetic resins, fibers and films by combination with glycols. The presence of p- 
toluic acid (p-TA), 4-carboxybenzaldehyde (4-CBA) and benzoic acid (BA) in pure terephthalic acid (PTA) used 
for the production of polyester is undesirable because they can slow down the polymerization process and 4- 
carboxybenzaldehyde (4-CBA) imparts coloration to the polymer due to thermal instability. Since the reaction 
medium is highly corrosive hence, anticorrosive reactors like titanium cladded reactors are generally used. 


Terephthalic Acid can affect, when breathed in. Contact can irritate the skin and eyes. Breathing Terephthalic 
Acid can irritate the nose, throat and lungs causing coughing, wheezing and/or shortness of breath. 


The standard was first published in 2001. In this (first) revision, test methods for determination of colour, 
determination of ash and determination of Acid Value have been modified, based on the latest technologies. HPLC 
method for determination of 4-carboxybenzaldehyde (4-CBA) and p-toluic acid (p-TA) content has also been 
modified. Normal voltage mode capillary electrophoresis test method for the determination of p-toluic acid, 4- 
carboxybenzaldehyde and benzoic acid in purified terephthalic acid and test method for determination of titanium 
in Annex E have been incorporated. Amendment no. | to IS 15030 : 2001 has been incorporated in this revision. 


Considerable assistance has been taken from the following test methods: 


a) ASTM D 7882 for determination of p-toluic acid (p-TA) and 4-carboxybenzaldehyde (4-CBA) in 
purified terephthalic acid (PTA) by normal voltage mode capillary electrophoresis; and 

b) ASTM D 7884 for determination of p-toluic acid (p-TA) and 4-carboxybenzaldehyde (4-CBA) in 
purified terephthalic acid (PTA) by high performance liquid chromatography. 


The composition of the Committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is given at Annex L. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 
2022 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (second revision). The number of significant places retained in the 
rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

1 SCOPE 


This standard prescribes requirements, the methods 
of sampling and test for pure terephthalic acid.

3 REQUIREMENTS 


3.1 Description 


The material shall be in the form of white crystalline 
free flowing powder and free from extraneous 
impurities like dust and dirt. Terephthalic is 
insoluble in water, chloroform, ether, acetic acid but 
slightly soluble in alcohol and completely soluble in 
alkalis. 


3.2 The material shall also comply with the 
requirements given in Table 1, when tested in 
accordance with the methods referred in col 4 of the 
Table 1.

4 PRECAUTIONS IN HANDLING 


Terephthalic acid has very low toxicity. The use of 
dust masks is advisable when handling terephthalic 
acid. Finely divided organic products which are 
combustible are liable to explosion should the dust 
content of the atmosphere be high and if ignition 
occurs. Good housekeeping is, therefore, advisable to 
minimize the amount of dust when terephthalic acid 
is handled. The atmosphere of any silo or pneumatic 
transfer equipment where dust explosions could 
occur should be blanketed with inert gas to below 10 
volume percent oxygen content. 


5 PACKING AND MARKING 


5.1 The material shall be supplied in bulk containers 
of 1 000 kg in flexible woven plastic or packages as 
agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 


5.2 Marking 


5.2.1 The packages shall be marked with the 
following: 


a) Name of the material, 

b) Name of manufacturer and his recognized 
trade-mark, if any; 

c) Month and year of manufacture; 

d) Net mass of the material in the container; 


e) Lot or batch number; and 
f) Any other statutory requirements. 


5.2.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The product(s) conforming to the requirements of this 
standard may be certified as per the conformity 
assessment schemes under the provisions of the 
Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the Rules 
and Regulations framed thereunder, and the products 
may be marked with the Standard Mark. 


6 SAMPLING 


The method of drawing representative samples of the 
material and the criteria for conformity shall be as 
prescribed in 4 of IS 5299. 


7 TEST METHODS 


7.1 Tests shall be conducted according to the method 
of test referred in col 4 of Table 1. 


7.2 Quality of Reagents 


Unless specified otherwise, “pure chemicals’ and 
distilled water (see IS 1070) shall be used in tests. 


NOTE — ‘Pure chemicals’ shall mean chemicals that do not 
contain impurities, which affect the results of analysis. 


IS 15030 : 2022 


ANNEX A 
[Table 1, SI No. (i)] 


DETERMINATION OF MOISTURE CONTENT 


A-1 GENERAL 


Moisture content is determined by using the karl 
fischer method. 


A-2 PROCEDURE 


Take about 2 g of the material and determine the 
moisture content by karl fischer method as described 
in IS 2362 


NOTE — Any other solvent system with appropriate ratio 
may be used for complete dissolution of pure terephthalic 
acid (PTA) while preparing the sample as prescribed in IS 
2362. 


ANNEX B 
[Table 1, SI No. (ii)] 


DETERMINATION OF COLOUR 


B-1 GENERAL 


Three methods namely, Methods A and C for 
determination of colour by visual comparison and 
Method B for determination of colour by tristimulus 
spectrophotometric method have been prescribed. In 
case of disputes, method B shall be the referee 
method. 


B-2 METHOD A 
B-2.1 General 


Colour of terephthalic acid solution in potassium 
hydroxide solution is measured using 2 M potassium 
hydroxide solution as reference on Pt-Co colour 
scale. 


B-2.2 Reagents 
B-2.2.1 Potassium Hydroxide, AR grade. 
B-2.2.2 Potassium Hydroxide Solution, 2 M. 


Take 56 g potassium hydroxide in 250 ml beaker and 
dissolve in distilled water. Transfer content in to 500 
ml volumetric flask and makeup the volume up to 
500 ml. 


NOTE — N, N-Dimethylformamide may be used as a blank 
in place of 2 M potassium hydroxide solution. 


B-2.3 Procedure 


Take 75 ml of 2 M potassium hydroxide solution in 
250 ml beaker and add magnetic stirrer bar. Slowly 
start stirring without splashing potassium hydroxide 
solution. Carefully add 10 + 0.1 g terephthalic acid 
slowly to beaker. Continue stirring till terephthalic 
acid is completely dissolved. 


Measure colour of terephthalic acid solution using 2 
M potassium hydroxide as blank by IS 8768 test 
method. 


Report colour as per IS 8768 test method. 


NOTE — Nessler tube of appropriate height may be used 
for testing as per IS 8768 


B-3 METHOD B 
B-3.1 Outline of the Method 


The sample is dissolved in aqueous potassium 
hydroxide and the colour of the solution is measured 
in Pt-Co units by using automatic tintometer that is 
tristimulus spectrophotometric method. 


B-3.2 Reagents 


B-3.2.1 Potassium Hydroxide Solution, 2 N 
aqueous. 


B-3.3 Apparatus 
B-3.3.1 Automatic Tintometer 
B-3.4 Calibration 


Prepare the instrument by following the instrument 
manufacturer’s instructions. Obtain a Pt-Co value of 
O for a sample of distilled water by instrument 
standardizing adjustments or program. It is 
advisable to read back distilled water to verify that 
the instrument reads a Pt-Co value of 0. Run quality 
assurance samples to verify the analytical system is 
in control. 


B-3.5 Procedure 


Take 75 ml of 2 N potassium hydroxide solution into 
a 250 ml beaker. Carefully, add 10.0 g of sample to 
it, with constant stirring to ensure complete 
dissolution. 


Measure the colour of solution by using 50 mm cell 
in automatic tintometer in Pt-Co colour mode. 


IS 15030 : 2022 


Testing of blank shall be done by using 2 N 
potassium hydroxide solution. 


NOTE — For effective mixing other tools like magnetic 
stirrer and sonication may be used. 


B-4 METHOD C 
B-4.1 Outline of the Method 


The colour of 5 percent solution of terephthalic acid 
in N, N-dimethylformamide is compared with that 
of the colour standard and expressed in terms of Pt- 
Co units. 


B-4.2 Apparatus 


B-4.2.1 Nessler Cylinder, two cylinder with 100 ml 
capacity each (see IS 4161). 


B-4.2.2 One-Mark Volumetric Flasks, 250 ml and 
500 ml capacities (see IS 915). 


B-4.2.3 Erlenmeyer Flask, 250 ml. 
B-4.3 Reagents 
B-4.3.1 Cobaltous Chloride Hexahydrate, solid. 


B-4.3.2 Concentrated Hydrochloric Acid (see IS 
265). 


B-4.3.3 Chloroplatinic Acid 


Dissolve 250 mg of platinum in small quantity of 
aqua regia contained in a glass or procelain dish by 
heating on a water-bath. When the metal has 
dissolved, evaporate the solution to dryness. Add 1 


ml of hydrochloric acid and again evaporate to 
dryness. Repeat this operation twice. 


B-4.3.4 N,N-Dimethylformamide 
B-4.4 Preparation of Colour Standard 


B-4.4.1 Dissolve 0.50 g of cobalt chloride 
hexahydrate and whole of the chloroplatinic acid 
(see B-4.3.3) in 50 ml of the hydrochloric acid. 
Warm, if necessary, to obtain a clear solution and 
after cooling, pour it into the 500 ml one-mark 
graduated flask. Dilute with water to the mark. This 
solution has a colour of 500 Pt-Co units. 


NOTE — Alternatively certified readymade standard may 
also be used. 


B-4.4.2 Pipette 5 ml of the solution (B-4.4.1) into a 
250 ml one-mark graduated flask and dilute with 
water to the mark. The diluted solution corresponds 
to a colour of 10 Pt-Co units and should always be 
freshly prepared. 


B-4.5 Procedure 


Weigh accurately 5.0 g of the material into a 250 ml 
erlenmeyer flask and add 100 + 0.5 ml of N, N- 
dimethylformamide. Shake the stoppered flask until 
all of the sample is dissolved. Transfer the solution 
into a nessler cylinder and compare the colour 
against a white background with the colour standard 
taken in the other nessler cylinder. The material shall 
be taken to have passed the test if the colour of the 
sample solution is not darker than that of the colour 
standard. 


IS 15030 : 2022 


ANNEX C 
[Table 1, SI No. (iii)] 


DETERMINATION OF ASH 


C-1 APPARATUS 
C-1.1 Muffle Furnace / Microwave Furnace 
C-1.2 Bunsen Burner, gas based or electric. 


C-1.3 Crucible, made of platinum or quartz or 
silica, 50 ml, or any suitable size. 


C-1.4 Analytical Balance 


C-1.5 Crucible Tongs, made of stainless steel with 
platinum tips. 


C-1.6 Glazed Porcelain Plates 

C-1.7 Clean glass beaker, 500 ml capacity. 
C-2 PROCEDURE 

C-2.1 Conditioning of Crucible 


Clean the crucible free from grease and salts by 
soaking in hot chromic acid or any other suitable 
acid, followed by distilled water. Place the crucible 
in the muffle furnace / microwave furnace kept at 
750°C with the help of platinum tipped crucible 
tongs for 30 min or till constant weight is achieved. 
Remove the crucible from the furnace and place it 
on a clean porcelain plate which is free of dust 
particles. Allow the crucible to cool for 1 min and 
transfer it to a desiccator which is placed near the 
analytical balance. 


Take the mass of the empty crucible nearest to 0.1 
mg. 


C-2.2 Sample for Ashing 


Take 500 ml capacity clean and dry beaker. Take 
around 100 + 50 g of terephthalic acid sample in 
beaker for ashing. Take mass of the beaker with 
terephthalic acid nearest to 0.1 g (W2). Use 
terephthalic acid in the beaker for ashing. After 
complete transfer of terephthalic acid for ashing in 
crucible further take mass of the beaker (W1). 


C-2.3 Sample Carbonization 


Place the pre-weighted crucible on a triangle 
supported by a tripod on Bunsen burner preferably 
in fume hood. Light Bunsen burner and allow to heat 
crucible. Add small quantity about 5-10 g of sample 
from beaker (C-2.2) and carbonize terephthalic 
sample. Continue adding terephthalic acid sample 
step by step to crucible till whole quantity of 
terephthalic acid sample is carbonized. 


C-2.4 Ashing of Terephthalic Acid Carbonized 
Residue 


After complete carbonization of whole terephthalic 
acid sample in crucible, keep the crucible in muffle 
furnace / microwave furnace kept at 750°C for 
minimum | h or till ashing is completed. All carbons 
must be removed during ashing process. Remove the 
crucible from the furnace and place it with ash in the 
desiccator for 30 min. Take the mass of the crucible 
and its contents nearest to 0.1 mg. 


NOTES 


1 External carbonization of terephthalic is not required 
when using temperature programmable microwave furnace. 
Many laboratories don’t use open flame inside laboratory 
for safety reason, programmable microwave furnace will 
provide options for such laboratories. 


2 A minimum of 100 + 50 g of sample is to be incinerated. 


3 Once the sample has been reduced to a carbonaceous ash, 
extreme care must be exercised in handling the crucible. If 
the crucible is handled in the usual manner with the tongs, 
carbon may be transferred to the tips of the tongs and may 
add carbon to the ash when the crucible is removed from the 
furnace. In order to prevent this source of serious error, turn 
the tongs with tips pointing upward and pick up the crucible 
by placing the arcs of the tongs around the body of the 
crucible. The crucible should not make contact with the 
refractory lining of the furnace as particles of platinum may 
be scratched off thus changing its mass. 


C-3 CALCULATION 


-MM1 rige

C-4 REPORT 


Report ash in terephthalic acid nearest to 1 ppm.

The material is dissolved in pyridine or dimethyl

and titrated with aqueous sodium hydroxide to 
phenolphthalein end point.

ANNEX E 


[Table 1, SI No. (v)] 
DETERMINATION OF IRON, COBALT, MANGANESE, CHROMIUM AND TITANIUM 


E-1 GENERAL 


The material is ashed in two separate dishes in 
presence of sulphuric acid. Ash in one dish is 
dissolved in concentrated hydrochloric acid and 
cobalt and manganese and titanium are determined 
by atomic absorption spectrophotometric method. 
Ash in the other dish is fused with potassium 
hydrogen sulphate, dissolved in concentrated 
hydrochloric acid and iron and chromium are 
determined by atomic absorption 
spectrophotometric method. In both cases 
air/acetylene flame is used. 


E-2 APPARATUS 


E-2.1 Atomic Absorption Spectrophotometer 
(AAS) 


For determination of these elements using AAS, 
details of test methods as given in relevant Indian 
Standard (see Annex J) maybe referred. Typical 
working conditions of AAS are given below for 
guidance only: 


Iron Cobalt Manganese Chromium Titanium 
Wavelength, nm 248.3 240.7 279.5 357.9 364.3 
HV 700 620 620 460 460

Fuel (acetylene) 6 6 6 6 6

Lamp current, mA 7 7 3 5 20 
Scale expansion 1 2 1 2 2 
Burner angle 0 0 0 0 0 


E-3 REAGENTS 


E-3.1 Concentrated Hydrochloric Acid (see IS 
265). 


E-3.2 Concentrated Sulphuric Acid (see IS 266). 
E-3.3 Potassium Hydrogen Sulphate, fine powder. 
E-3.4 Stock Iron Solution, 1 000 ppm (™m/). 

E-3.5 Stock Cobalt Solution, 1 000 ppm (m/v). 
E-3.6 Stock Manganese Solution, 1 000 ppm (m/v). 
E-3.7 Stock Chromium Solution, 1 000 ppm (m/). 
E-3.8 Stock Titanium Solution, 1 000 ppm (m/). 


E-4 PREPARATION OF 
SOLUTIONS 


STANDARD 


E-4.1 Standard Working Solutions 


Pipette 10.0 ml of each of the stock solutions 
(E-3.4 to E-3.8) into a 1 000 ml flask and make up 
to the mark to give 10 ppm (m/v) standard working 
solutions. These shall be prepared fresh every time 
before testing. 


E-4.1.1 Standard Iron, Chromium and Titanium 
solutions 


Take 5, 10, 15 and 20 ml of standard working 
solutions of iron, chromium and titanium of 10 ppm 
(m/v) (E-4.1) in each of four 100 ml volumetric 
flasks. Add 1 g of ground potassium hydrogen 
sulphate and 5 percent hydrochloric acid and shake 
to dissolve. Dilute to the mark with 5 percent 
hydrochloric acid (HCl) to give standard solutions 
containing 0.5, 1.0, 1.5 and 2.0 ppm (m/v) of iron, 
chromium and titanium. 


E-4.1.2 Standard Cobalt and Manganese Solutions 


Take 5, 10, 15 and 20 ml of both standard working 
solutions of cobalt and manganese of 10 ppm (m/v) 
(E-4.1) in each of four 100 ml volumetric flasks. 
Make up to the mark with 5 percent hydrochloric 
acid (HCl) and shake well. This gives standard 


solutions containing 0.5, 1.0, 1.5 and 2.0 ppm (m/v) 
of cobalt and manganese. 


E-5 PROCEDURE 


E-5.1 Weigh accurately about 25 g of sample into 
two separate silica (or platinum or quartz) dishes. 
Wet thoroughly with 5 ml of concentrated sulphuric 
acid and char completely under a vertical heater or 
by using hot plate. Place the dishes in the entrance 
of a muffle furnace with the door open, and fume 
until most of the carbon has been removed. Move 
the dishes further into the muffle furnace, close the 
door gently and leave until all the carbon has been 
removed. Care shall be taken that the sample does 
not ignite. 


E-5.2 Add 5 ml of concentrated hydrochloric acid 
to one of the dishes, warm, if necessary, to dissolve 
and transfer quantitatively to a 100 ml volumetric 
flask. Make up to the mark with water. Run through 
in following order; respective standards; samples 
and standards again for cobalt and manganese using 
given conditions (see E-2.1). 


E-5.3 Fuse the residue from the other dish with 1.00 
g of ground potassium hydrogen sulphate (KHSO,) 
and a few drops of concentrated sulphuric acid over 
a bunsen burner or hot plate. Cool and add 5 ml of 
concentrated hydrochloric acid, warm, if necessary 
to dissolve and transfer quantitatively to a 100 ml 
volumetric flask and make up to the mark with 
water. Prepare a blank by taking 1.0 g of ground 
potassium hydrogen sulphate (KHSO4) and a few 
drops of concentrated sulphuric acid. Run through in 
following order respective standards; blank 
samples and standards again for iron and chromium 
and titanium, using the given conditions (see E-2.1). 


E-6 CALCULATION 


The respective metals (that is iron, chromium,

ANNEX F 
[Table 1, SI No. (vi)] 


DETERMINATION OF SODIUM, MAGNESIUM, POTASSIUM, CALCIUM AND NICKEL 


F-1 PRINCIPLE 


The sample is ashed in the presence of sulphuric 
acid. The ash is dissolved in concentrated 
hydrochloric acid. Concentration of sodium, 
potassium, and nickel are determined by atomic 
absorption spectrophotometry in an air/acetylene 
flame. Concentration of calcium and magnesium are 
determined by atomic absorption spectrophotometry 
in a nitrous oxide/acetylene flame. 


F-2 APPARATUS 
F-2.1 Atomic Absorption Spectrophotometer 


For determination of these elements using AAS, 
details of test methods as given in relevant Indian 
Standard (see Annex J) may be referred. Typical 
conditions only for guidance are given below. The 
wavelengths given are the true atomic line 
wavelengths and may not correspond exactly to the 
wavelength dial of the instrument 


Sodium Nickel Calcium Magnesium Potassium

Band pass, nm 0.5 0.15 0.5 0.5 2 
Burner height, nm 7 7 7 7 7 
Oxidant air Air N.O N20 N20 N20 
Lamp current, mA 4 7 5 4 X

Integration time, s 1 1 1 1 1 


*Emission mode 


F-3 REAGENTS 

F-3.1 Hydrochloric Acid (see IS 265). 

F-3.2 Sulphuric Acid (see IS 266). 

F-3.3 Stock Sodium Solution, 1 000 ppm (m/v). 
F-3.4 Stock Potassium Solution, 1 000 ppm (m/v). 
F-3.5 Stock Calcium Solution, 1 000 ppm (m/v). 


F-3.6 Stock Magnesium Solution, 1 000 ppm 
(m/v). 


F-3.7 Stock Nickel Solution, 1 000 ppm (m/v). 


F-4 PREPARATION OF 
SOLUTIONS 


STANDARD 


F-4.1 Standard Working Solutions 


Pipette 10 ml of each of the stock solutions (F-3.3 to 
F-3.7) into 1 000 ml flask and dilute each to the mark 
to give 10 ppm (m/v) of standard working solution. 
These shall be prepared fresh every day before 
testing. 


F-4.1.1 Standard Sodium, Potassium, Calcium, 
Magnesium and Nickel Solutions 


Take 10 ml concentrated hydrochloric acid into each 
of the five 100 ml volumetric flasks. Add by means 
of pipette 2, 5, 10, 20 and 50 ml of each of the 
standard working solutions (see F-4.1) into each of 
the volumetric flasks and dilute to the mark with 
water to give standard solutions of 0.2, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0 
and 5.0 ppm (m/v) of each of the elements. Prepare 
a zero-standard solution by pipetting 10 ml of 
concentrated hydrochloric acid into a 100 ml 
volumetric flask and diluting to the mark with 
demineralized water.

a temperature-controlled heater or microwave 
oven/furnace. Prepare a blank by adding 5 ml of

ANNEX G 


[Table 1, SI No. (v) and (vi)] 
METAL ANALYSIS IN TEREPHTHALIC ACID BY ICP-OES TECHNIQUE 


G-1 GENERAL 


G-1.1 This test method covers determination of iron, 
cobalt, manganese, chromium, titanium, sodium, 
magnesium, potassium, calcium and nickel in the 
concentration range of 0.1 mg/kg to 10 mg/kg in 
terephthalic acid by inductively coupled plasma 
optical emission spectrometry method (ICP-OES). 
Higher metal content may also be analyzed by ICP- 
AES method by appropriate dilution. 


NOTE — ICP-OES and ICP-AES is synonym of analytical 
technique. 


G-2 OUTLINE OF THE TEST METHOD 


Terephthalic acid sample is either dissolved in 
ammonium hydroxide or ashed, fused, digested and 
dissolved in aqueous solution. Metals are analyzed 
by internal standard method. Alternatively, metals 
can also be analyzed by external calibration 
technique. 


After dilution, the solution is aspirated into the 
plasma of an inductively coupled plasma emission 
spectrometer and emission radiation of the 
resonance lines of the elements under analysis is 


measured and compared with a curve constructed 
from standard calibration solution. 


G-3 APPARATUS 


G-3.1 Analytical Balance, minimum capacity 200 
g capable of weighing to the nearest 0.1 mg. 


G-3.2 Inductively Coupled Plasma Atomic 
Emission Spectrometer 


Either a sequential or simultaneous spectrometer is 
suitable, if equipped with a quartz inductively 
coupled plasma (ICP) torch and radio frequency 
(RF) generator to form and sustain the plasma. 


G-3.3 Nebulizer, reduces the possibility of clogging 
and minimizes aerosol particle effects. Any 
manufacturer’s recommend suitable nebulizer may 
be used. 


G-3.4 Peristaltic Pump 


A peristaltic pump is recommended to provide a 
constant flow of solution. The pumping speed shall 
be in the range of 0.5 to 3 ml/min. The pump tubing 
shall withstand at least 6 h exposure to the dilution 


IS 15030 : 2022 


solvent. Alternatively, any latest peristatic pump 
with instrument suppliers’ specification may also be 
used. 


G-3.5 Crucible/Dish, made of platinum or silica or 
quartz, 50 ml capacity, minimum. 


G-3.6 Hot Plate, with or without magnetic stirring 
capability. 


G-3.7 Muffle Furnace or Microwave Muffle 
Furnace, capable of being maintained at 
temperatures of (750 + 25)°C. 


G-4 REAGENTS 


G-4.1 Distilled Water/Ultrapure Water, for 
dilution of certified reference material (CRM) for 
preparation of the calibration standards/samples and 
for use as blank. 


G-4.2 Hydrochloric Acid, 
percent purity, minimum. 


concentrated, 36 


G-4.3 Sulphuric Acid, concentrated 98 percent 
purity, minimum. 


G-4.4 Nitric Acid 


G-4.5 Internal Standard, yttrium or scandium 
(or any suitable metal) is used for internal 
standardization. 


G-4.6 Single or Multi Element Certified 
Reference Material (Standard) 


G-4.7 Di-lithium-tetraborate 


G-4.8 High Purity Argon Gas, analytical grade, 
purity 99.99 percent, minimum. 


G-4.9 Ammonia Solution, 25 percent, minimum. 


NOTE — Analytical grade chemicals shall be used. It is 
intended that all reagents conform to the metal-free and the 
reagent is of sufficiently high purity to permit its use 
without lessening the accuracy of the determination. 


G-5 SAMPLE 
PREPARATION 


AND STANDARD 


G-5.1 Sample preparation 


Terephthalic acid sample is either dissolved in 
ammonium hydroxide (see G-5.1.1) or 
ashed/fused/digested (see G-5.1.2.1 or G-5.1.2.2) 
and dissolved in aqueous solution. Metals are 
analyzed by internal standard method. 


G-5.1.1 Terephthalic acid sample dissolution in 
ammonium hydroxide solution 


G-5.1.1 Terephthalic acid sample dissolution in 
ammonium hydroxide solution 


G-5.1.1.1 Take 3-7 g of PTA powder in 100 ml 
volumetric flask, add 15-20 ml of water, 0.2 ppm 
yttrium (as internal standard) and 4-15 ml of 
ammonia solution (25-30 percent) solution. 
Sonicate till complete powder is dissolved. Make up 
the solution up to 100 ml with distilled water. 


G-5.1.1.2 To prepare blank solution, follow the 
above procedure (see G-5.1.1.1) except addition of 
PTA powder. 


G-5.1.2 Terephthalic acid sample is ashed and 
dissolved in aqueous solution 


5.1.2.1 Ashing followed by fusing and digestion by 
using microwave furnace/ muffle furnace followed 
by ICP-OES 


G-5.1.2.1.1 Weigh accurately about 100 g of sample 
(or appropriate quantity suitable for precise metal 
analysis) in crucible/dish. Wet thoroughly with 
about 5-10 ml of concentrated sulphuric acid and 
char completely by keeping crucible/dish on hot 
plate at low heat for about 5-10 min. Place the 
crucible/dish in the microwave furnace/ muffle 
furnace until all the carbon has been completely 
removed. Remove crucible/dish from furnace and 
cool in desiccator. 


G-5.1.2.1.2 Fuse the residue from the crucible/dish 
with 1 g of ground di-lithium-tetraborate and a few 
drops of concentrated sulphuric acid over a bunsen 
burner or hot plate. Cool and add 5 ml of 
concentrated hydrochloric acid, warm, if necessary 
to dissolve and transfer quantitatively to a 100 ml 
volumetric flask and make it up to the mark with 
distilled water and analyze by ICP-OES. 


G-5.1.2.1.3 Prepare a blank by taking 1.0 g of 
ground di-lithium-tetraborate and a few drops of 
concentrated sulphuric acid. 


G-5.1.2.2 Ashing by using microwave furnace/ 
muffle furnace followed by ICP-OES 


Place 75 + 25 g of PTA in the crucible/dish. Weigh 
the crucible/dish and contents on the analytical 
balance to the nearest 0.1 g and record the net weight 
of the PTA. Place the dish in the microwave furnace/ 
muffle furnace for | h at 750°C until the entire black 
residue has been burned off. Dissolve PTA ash in 
nitric acid and transfer to a 100 ml volumetric flask 
and make it up to the mark with distilled water and 
analyze by ICP-OES. 


G-5.2 Standard Preparation 
Prepare minimum two matrix match calibration 


standard using either multi-element standard or 
single element standards and calibrate ICP 


instrument. Calibration range should 
concentration of metal in sample solution. 


cover 


If analysis is done by internal standard method, 
internal standard is added to the sample and standard 
solutions to compensate for variations in test 
specimen introduction efficiency. By comparing 
emission intensities measured with the standards, 
the concentrations of elements in the test specimen 
are calculated. Add 0.2 ppm yttrium (another 


IS 15030 : 2022 


appropriate internal standard may also be used) as 
an internal standard in all matrix calibration standard 
include blank. 


NOTE — Ensure that there should not be any precipitation 
in sample as well as in calibration standard. In case of 
ammonia dilution method, use of ammonium hydroxide is 
optional in calibration mixture.

ANNEX H 
[Table 1, SI No. (vii) and (viii)] 


DETERMINATION OF 4- CARBOXYBENZALDEHYDE (4-CBA) AND p-TOLUIC ACID (p-TA) 


H-1 GENERAL 


Four methods namely, Method A, Method B, 
Method C and Method D have been prescribed. 
Method A for the determination of 4- 
carboxybenzaldehyde (4-CBA) and p-toluic acid (p- 
TA) by high-performance liquid chromatography 
(HPLC) method, Method B for the determination of 
p-toluic acid (p-TA) in pure terephthalic acid by gas 
chromatographic (GC) method, Method C for the 
determination of 4-carboxybenzaldehyde (4-CBA) 
in pure terephthalic acid using poloragraphic 
analyzer and Method D for the determination of p- 
toluic acid (p-TA) and 4-carboxybenzaldehyde (4- 
CBA) in purified terephthalic acid (PTA) by normal 
voltage mode capillary electrophoresis (CE). 
Method A, Method C and Method D may be used 
for determination of 4-carboxybenzaldehyde (4- 
CBA) and Method A, Method B and Method D may 
be used for determination of p-toluic acid (p-TA). 


H-2 METHOD A DETERMINATION OF 4- 
CARBOXYBENZALDEHYDE (4-CBA) AND p- 
TOLUIC ACID (p-TA) BY HPLC METHOD 


H-2.1 General 


4-Carboxybenzaldehyde (4-CBA) of concentration 
ranging from 2 to 500 ppm (w/v) and p-toluic acid 
(p-TA) of concentration ranging from 10 to 500 ppm 
(w/w) in purified terephthalic acid (PTA) is 
determined by reverse phase high performance 
liquid chromatography (HPLC). 


H-2.2 Summary of Test Method 


The PTA sample is dissolved in ammonium 
hydroxide solution and injected into a high- 
performance liquid chromatograph with a UV 
detector in a fixed volume. The impurities of p-TA 
and 4-CBA are separated from PTA using a C18 
chemically bonded column. For quantification, an 
external standard calibration is used. 


H-2.3 Apparatus 


H-2.3.1 HPLC System, capable of pumping the 
mobile phase at flow rates between 0.1 and 2.0 
ml/min, pressure between 0 and 40 MPa and a 
pulsation of less than | percent full scale deflection 
under the test conditions described in Table 2. The 
S/N (signal to noise) ratio should be greater than or 
equal to 3:1 for 2 ppm (w/v) 4-CBA and 10 ppm 
(w/w) p-TA.

H-2.3.3 Detector, variable wavelength ultraviolet

H-2.3.4 Column Oven, any suitable HPLC column

H-2.4 Reagents

percent. 


H-2.4.2 Phosphoric Acid (H3PO04), HPLC grade. 
H-2.4.3 Acetonitrile, HPLC grade. 

H-2.4.4 Water, HPLC grade. 

H-2.4.5 Ammonium Hydroxide Solution 


Take 1 volume of ammonium hydroxide and 1 
volume of water. 


H-2.4.6 PTA Standard for Calibration 


A certified PTA calibration standard with known 
amounts of p-TA and 4-CBA is required. In case of 
non-availability of PTA calibrated standard, the 
concentrations of p-TA and 4-CBA in a PTA sample 
can be determined by procedure mentioned at H-2.5. 
The calibrated PTA sample may be used as a PTA 
calibration standard. 


H-2.4.7 Mobile Phase 


H-2.4.7.1 0.06 Percent Phosphoric Acid (H3PO4) 
solution : acetonitrile (82:18) 


To make 0.06 percent phosphoric acid (H3PO4) 
solution, pipette 0.6 ml phosphoric acid into a 1 000 
ml volumetric flask make up to the mark with water. 
Mix 820 ml of phosphoric acid solution and 180 ml 
of acetonitrile. In the mobile phase, methanol could 
be used instead of acetonitrile. 


NOTE — Degassing and filtering of the mobile phase is 
recommended before use; degassing can be done on-line or 
off-line by helium sparging, vacuum degassing or ultrasonic 
agitation. 


H-2.5 Procedure for Calibration of PTA Sample 
by Individual Components 


H-2.5.1 To determine the concentrations of p-TA 
and 4-CBA, a PTA sample with granularity of 80 to 
160 um, containing 4-CBA and p-TA at 
concentrations of 10 to 25 ppm and 100 to 200 ppm, 
respectively, are to be analyzed. This PTA sample 
with calibrated concentrations of p-TA and 4-CBA 
can be used as the PTA standard for sample analysis.

98.0 percent, minimum. 


H-2.5.3 4-CBA (10 ug/ml) Calibration Standard

concentration 500 ppm. Then dilute with water 50 
times to 10 ug/ml. 


H-2.5.4 p-TA (80 ug/ml, w/w) Calibration Standard

prepared in H-2.5.3. Then dilute with water to 80 


ug/ml.

H-3 METHOD B DETERMINATION OF p- 
TOLUIC ACID (p-TA) IN PURE 
TEREPHTHALIC ACID BY GAS 
CHROMATQGRAPHIC METHOD 


H-3.1 General 

This method is used for the determination of p-toluic 
acid (p-TA) in terephthalic acid in the range of 0- 
200 ppm. 


H-3.2 Summary of the Method 


hydroxide solution and injected into an injector 
(pyrolysis unit). The resulting esters are then 
separated by gas chromatography using a heart cut 
system for estimation of the p-toluic acid content. 


H-3.3 Principle 


Pure terephthalic acid dissolved in tetramethy- 
lammonium hydroxide (TMA) is injected in 
pyrolysis block maintained (400 + 5)°C. All the 
acids get converted into respective esters. Thus, p- 
toluic acid gets converted to methyl-p-toluate 
(MPT). 


IS 15030 : 2022 


This methyl-p-toluate (MPT) is determined by 
separation technique on GC column using heart cut 
system. 


H-3.4 Apparatus 
H-3.4.1 Gas Chromatography 


Any suitable gas chromatography with flame 
ionization detector equipped with heart-cutting 
system with a pyrolysis unit heated to 400°C. 
Integrator A suitable computing integrator and 
syringe microliter syringe of 10 ul size. 


H-3.4.1.1 Chromatographic Column 


a) Pre-column — 3.18 mm Stainless steel 1 m 
column packed with 10 percent SP-1000 on 
80-100 mesh AW Chromosorb W or 
equivalent 


b) Main-column — 3.18 mm Stainless steel 2 
m column packed with 10 percent SP-1000 on 
80-100 mesh AW Chromosorb W or 
equivalent 


H-3.4.1.2 Column Conditioning 


Condition the column before use for 12 h having 
nitrogen carrier flow of 30 ml/min.

Carrier gas Nitrogen 


H-3.6.2 Energize the solenoid valve manually via 
push buttons on flow switching unit (FSU) and set 
the primary nitrogen regulator (stream 1) to the 1.9 
kg/cm? (27 psig). At this time secondary nitrogen 
regulator must be turned off and heart cut needle 
valve (in FSU) should be fully open. Allow the 
system to attain equilibrium that may take about 15- 
20 min and note the natural mid-point pressure 
(secondary nitrogen/stream 2 pressure gauge). 
Measure the carrier gas flow rate at FID vent (Air/H2 
off). It should be 5 ml in 14.0 + 0.1 s by bubble flow 
meter. If it is not so, adjust the flow using PF 
(premium regulator 1). De-energize the solenoid 
valve manually by push bottom on FSU. Now the 
mid-point pressure will decrease gradually via the 
heart cut vent. Using secondary nitrogen pressure 
regulator (PR2), increase the mid-point pressure to 
3.447 kPa (0.5 psig) greater than the noted natural 
mid-point pressure. With the solenoid valve 
energized, measure the flow rate at the FID vent 
(Air/H. off). Note this value. De-energize the 
solenoid valve and adjust the heart cut needle valve 
to give a flow rate equal to measured at FID vent that 
is 5 ml in 12.0 min. 


NOTE — To achieve the above-mentioned rate, slight 


variation in pressure may be necessary, if pressure required 
to check for column leaks, septum leak, etc is higher. 


H-3.6.3 Set the FID air and hydrogen to the flow 
rates below: 


Hydrogen pressure = 0.75 kg/cm? (10.5 
psig) = 31.3 ml/min + 5.0 


Air pressure = 0.45 kg/cm? (6.5 psig) = 
258.6 ml/ min + 10.0 


H-3.6.4 Light the flame and allow the system to 
stabilize overnight.

H-4 METHOD C DETERMINATION OF 4- 
CARBOXYBENZALDEHYDE IN PURE 
TEREPHTHALIC ACID USING 
POLORAGRAPHIC ANALYZER 


H-4.1 General 


This method is for the determination of 4-carboxy 
benzaldehyde (4-CBA) in pure terephthalic acid 
(PTA) in the range 0 to 50 ppm. 


H-4.2 Summary of the Method 


The sample is dissolved in 1 M potassium hydroxide 
solution and 0.01 percent polyethylene glycol 6 000 
(PEG 6 000) is added. After deoxygenating with 
nitrogen, the differential pulse polarogram is 


IS 15030 : 2022 


recorded and the height of the carbonyl reduction 
wave at —1.32 V (relative to a saturated calomel 
electrode) is measured. This peak height is 
proportional to the concentration of 4-CBA in the 
sample and from a calibration graph, constructed 
using standard solutions, the concentrations of 4- 
CBA is determined. 


H-4.3 Principle 


Polarographic technique is used for those 
components in solution that can be 
electrochemically oxidized or reduced. In this 
potential (voltage) is applied to sample via a 
conductive electrode that is dropping mercury 
electrode which is also called as working electrode. 
Potential is scanned over region of interest, much as 
the wavelength of light is scanned in spectroscopic 
measurements. When component is 
reduced/oxidized at particular potential current will 
flow at working electrode and the potential at which 
the current is one half the diffusion value is half 
wave potential E'/>. This El, is characteristic of 
particular substance undergoing reaction and is 
useful in identifying the solution constituents. Table 
of Elf, values for various organic and inorganic 
species is available in reference books. 


For determination of 4-CBA, differential pulse 
polarographic technique is used in which voltage is 
applied to the cell in pulses. Current produced after 
reduction of 4-CBA is measured twice for each drop, 
first just before pulse is applied and second just 
before pulse ends. The difference in two readings is 
signal which is fed to X-Y flatbed recorder and peak 
proportional to concentration of 4-CBA is recorded. 


H-4.4 Interference 


Dissolved oxygen is expelled from the test solution 
with inert gas such as argon or nitrogen or otherwise 
polarogram of dissolve oxygen will interfere with 
the sample. Polyethylene glycol 16 000 is added 
in test solution to suppress the polarographic 
maximum which normally interferes in peak of 
interest. 


H-4.5 Apparatus 


A suitable polarographic analyzer fitted with 
dropping mercury electrode and XY flatbed 
recorder. 


H-4.6 Reagents 
H-4.6.1 Potassium Hydroxide Solution, 1 M. 


Dissolve 330 g of potassium hydroxide, AR grade in 
water and make up to 5 1. 


H-4.6.2 Pure Terephthalic Acid (TA). 
Containing lea than 5 ppm 4-CBA is suitable. 


H-4.6.3 Polyethylene Glycol 6 000 (PEG 6 000) 
solution, | percent (m/v) 


Dissolve 1.0 g of PEG 6 000, GR grade in water and 
make upto 100 ml in standard flask shake well to 
ensure complete solution. 


H-4.6.4 4-Carboxybenzaldehyde, AR Grade, 99 
percent purity. 


H-4.7 Calibration Standard 


H-4.7.1 Weigh 0.100 0 g of pure 4-CBA into 50 ml 
beaker. Add approximately 30 ml of 1 M potassium 
hydroxide and stir to dissolve. Quantitatively 
transfer this solution to a 100 ml volumetric flask; 
and dilute to mark, with | M potassium hydroxide. 
Call this solution ‘A’. 


1 ml solution ‘A’= 1 mg 4-CBA. 


H-4.7.2 Pipette 10 ml of solution A into 100 ml 
volumetric flask and dilute to the mark with 1 M 
potassium hydroxide. Call this solution ‘B’. 


1 ml solution B = 100 ug 4-CBA. 


NOTES 


1 Solution A and B are not stable and should be made as and 
when required. 


2 If 4-CBA is dissolved in warm potassium hydroxide 
solution, yellow colour can occur, indicative of chemical 
reaction. If this occurs, 4-CBA solution should be discarded 
and cold potassium hydroxide solution should be used 
before making standard. 


3 Argon/Nitrogen, approximately 10.342 1 kPa (1.5 psi) for 
16 min to ensure absence of oxygen peak. 


4 Mercury, polarographic grade or AR grade. 


CAUTION — As mercury is very poisonous and its 
vapours are harmful, mercury should be handled very 
carefully. If any spillage occurs, mercury should be 
removed immediately using vacuum. 


H-4.8 Calibration 
H-4.8.1 Three-point Calibration 


Into six 100 ml volumetric flasks weigh 5.00 g of 
pure terephthalic acid (TA). Pipette 1 ml of 1 percent 
(m/v) PEG 6 000 solution into each flask and add 
approximately 75 ml of 1 M potassium hydroxide. 
Stopper the flasks and shake vigorously, to dissolve 
terephthalic acid (TA). To series of 100 ml flasks 
add from pipette 0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5 ml of 
solution B respectively. Make upto the mark with 1 
M potassium hydroxide. Shake well to mix and then 
record the polarogram for each standard as described 


in procedure. Plot a calibration curve of ug 4-CBA 
v/s peak height (corrected for blank). Calculate the 
mean factor as F = VSlope.

H-4.9.2 Sample Preparation 


Transfer quantitatively 5.0 + 0.01 g of pure 
terephthalic acid into 100 ml volumetric flask. 
Pipette 1 ml of 1 percent (m/v) PEG 6 000 solution 
to the flask. Add 75 ml of 1 M potassium hydroxide 
and stopper the flask. Shake vigorously till all 
terephthalic acid (TA) is dissolved. Make up to the 
mark with 1 M potassium hydroxide and mix well. 
Pour approximately 12 ml of this solution into 


This method is used for the determination of p-toluic 
acid (p-TA) and 4-carboxybenzaldehyde (4-CB A) in 
purified terephthalic acid (PTA) by capillary 
electrophoresis (CE) with normal voltage mode and 
UV detection. It is applicable for p-toluic acid (p- 
TA) in the range of 10 to 400 ppm (w/w) and for 4- 
carboxybenzaldehyde (4-CBA) in the range of 5 to 
400 ppm (w/w). 


H-5.2 Summary of Test Method 


The sample is dissolved in ammonium hydroxide 
solution. p-toluic acid, 4-carboxybenzaldehyde 
and terephthalic acid gets dissociate and become 
homologous ions under basic conditions. Using 
hydrodynamic sampling, a fixed amount of this 
solution is introduced into the capillary. A voltage 
is applied to the capillary to separate the 
impurities, p-TA and 4-CBA from PTA. External 
standard calibration is used for quantification.

H-5.3.1 Capillary Electrophoresis System (see 
Fig. 3 for components)

H-5.3.1.1 High voltage power supply, which can

may be used as a PTA calibration standard.

H-5.5 Procedure for Calibration of PTA sample

H-5.5.1 To determine the concentrations of p-TA

respectively, are to be analysed. This PTA sample 


with calibrated concentrations of p-TA and 4-CBA 
can be used as the PTA standard for sample analysis.

H-5.5.3 4-CBA (10 ug/ml) Calibration Standard

of ammonium hydroxide solution, and stir until 4- 
CBA is completely dissolved. Then accurately 
transfer the resulting solution to a 50 ml volumetric 
flask and dilute to the mark with water to make the 
concentration 500 ppm. Then dilute with water 50 
times to 10 ppm. 


H-5.5.4 p-TA (80 ug/ml) Calibration Standard.

TA and prepare 400 ppm p-TA standard solution as 
prepared in H-5.5.3. Then dilute with water to 80 


ppm.

correlation coefficient) greater than or equal to 
0.995 is derived; if not, the whole procedure is to be 
repeated. To interpret the calibration, a computer or 
data system may also be used (see Fig 4).

H-5.6.2 A constant temperature is to be maintained 
in capillary electrophoresis system. The electrolyte 
reservoir is filled with fresh electrolyte working 
solution and is allowed to stand for 10 min for 
obtaining thermal equilibrium. A new capillary prior 
to use is to be conditioned with 0.5 mol/l sodium 
hydroxide solution for 5 min, followed by water for 
5 min. Then the capillary is purged with electrolyte 
for 3 min. Current is tested by applying 15 kV 
voltage. If there is no current, the capillary may have 
a bubble, a blockage, or both. Retry after degassing 
the electrolyte working solution. Replace the 
capillary if there is still no current. Set the UV 
detector to a detection wavelength of 200 nm, or 
equivalent and the absorbance value to 0.000. UV 
offset is less than 0.1 AU. For normal voltage mode, 
programme the CE system with a constant voltage 
of + (15-25) kV. Set up the CE system for a 
hydrodynamic sampling. Different sampling times 
are acceptable as long as the samples and standards 
are analyzed in the same way. Allow the CE system 
to run for 10 min and 6 min. Between each analaysis, 


22, 


purge with water and electrolyte in series. Set the 
data system’s acquisition rate to at least 20 points/s. 
Program the data system such that analyte peaks are 
identified based on migration time, and peak area is 
used to quantify analyte peak response. 


H-5.7 Procedure 
H-5.7.1 Calibration 


In a 100 ml volumetric flask, weigh 2.0 g of PTA 
standard (to the nearest 0.000 1 g), add 4 ml 
ammonium hydroxide solution (H-5.4.7) and 50 ml 
distilled water and stir until PTA is completely 
dissolved. Then dilute it to the mark with water. 
Inject a small amount of the calibration standard 
solution into the CE for analysis once 
steady operating conditions are achieved. Using the 
data system, record electropherograms and peak 
area values for p-TA and 4-CBA. Calculate the 
average peak area after analysing the calibration 
standard three times. 


NOTE — To dissolve PTA in ammonium hydroxide 
solution magnetic stirrer or ultrasonic bath can also be used. 


H-5.7.2 Analysis of samples 


Weigh about 2.0 to 4.0 g PTA sample (to the nearest 
0.000 1 g) and repeat other procedures given at H-

5.7.1. Record the peak area values of p-TA and 4- 
CBA. Run the sample. Rinse the capillary with 
water for 10 min and then with electrolyte for 6 min, 
after each assay. Electropherogram of a PTA sample 
is given in Fig. 5.

in PTA standard;

H-5.9.2 Report the following information in the

a) The complete identification of the sample 
tested; 

b) Any deviation from the prescribed process 
(for example, detailed description of column 
and operating conditions); 

c) Results of the test; and 


d) Any unusual circumstances discovered 
throughout the test.

Check that the drain fitting is secured on the 
spray chamber drain. Loose fitting drain 
can cause pressure leaks and plasma 
instability. 


Check that the peristaltic pump tubing is in 
good condition, has no flat spots and is 
correctly installed around the pump head. 


Check that the spray chamber drain is 
properly set up on the pump so that waste 
is pumped out of the spray chamber.

drain underneath the sample shelf lead to 
the drain bottle. Empty the drain - bottle if 
necessary. Dispose off waste properly.

Bureau of Indian Standards 


BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 to promote harmonious 
development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to 
connected matters in the country. 


Copyright 


BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without 
the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the 
standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to 
copyright be addressed to the Head (Publication & Sales), BIS. 


Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the website- 
www.bis.gov.in or www.standardsbis.in. 


This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc No.: PCD 09 (18966).
